canonical.title: The hard parts of React forms in 2026: arrays, conditionals, wizards, and the render budget

siblings.title: The React form-library landscape in 2026: RHF still wins, TanStack Form is the real challenger, Formik is a zombie
siblings.summary: React Hook Form (v7.81.0, 58M weekly downloads, v8 in beta) remains the default; TanStack Form 1.33.2 is the credible challenger; Conform owns progressive-enhancement forms; Formik is a zombie.

siblings.title: React's native form primitives in 2026: what they replace, and what they don't
siblings.summary: React's form primitives are a submission layer, not a form layer — they own pending/error/optimistic state across the network boundary, and own nothing about the fields.

siblings.title: The validation & schema layer for React forms in 2026: Zod 4, Valibot, ArkType
siblings.summary: Standard Schema v1 turned the schema library into a swappable dependency; Zod 4 stays the default, Valibot wins the client bundle, ArkType wins raw throughput.

siblings.title: Wiring form engines into React UI kits in 2026
siblings.summary: The UI kits stopped picking a form engine for you; the real cost is the per-component Controller/field.state bridge you still hand-write.

siblings.title: Testing React forms in 2026: which tier catches what
siblings.summary: Vitest + schema unit tests + jsdom component tests, with Browser Mode as the real middle tier and Playwright reserved for the flows that touch the network.

siblings.title: Uploads, autosave and unsaved-changes guards in React forms (2026)
siblings.summary: Bytes bypass your form: the browser presigns and uploads direct-to-storage while the form only carries a key — and progress still means XHR, not fetch.

sources.title: https://react-hook-form.com/docs/usefieldarray
sources.claim: useFieldArray API surface (append/prepend/insert/swap/move/update/replace/remove) and its hard rules: field.id as key, no flat field arrays, shouldUnregister:true unsupported, append requires full defaults, don't stack actions.

sources.title: https://deepwiki.com/react-hook-form/react-hook-form/5.3-advanced-field-array-patterns
sources.claim: Nested field arrays require one useFieldArray per level keyed on the parent index; parent remove/swap/move propagate to nested arrays via control._subjects.array; shouldUnregister governs whether unmounted array data survives.

sources.title: https://react-hook-form.com/docs/useform/register
sources.claim: register supports a `deps` option that triggers validation of dependent inputs; only dot path syntax is supported; shouldUnregister should be avoided with useFieldArray.

sources.title: https://react-hook-form.com/migrate-v7-to-v8
sources.claim: RHF v8 beta adds first-class React Compiler support and flat field arrays; renames field id to key, removes keyName, removes the watch callback API in favour of subscribe, and stops setValue from updating field arrays (use replace).

sources.title: https://react-hook-form.com/docs/useform/subscribe
sources.claim: RHF's subscribe() lets you observe formState and values without triggering a render, and is the replacement for the watch callback.

sources.title: https://react-hook-form.com/advanced-usage
sources.claim: RHF's official wizard recipe stores cross-step data in an external store (little-state-machine) with one useForm per route; FormProvider re-renders the subtree on state updates; virtualized lists need form-level defaultValues so rows restore on remount.

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/react-hook-form/discussions/7810
sources.claim: RHF field arrays with 100+ fields go laggy when formState is subscribed at the root; maintainer attributes it to dirtyFields updates re-rendering the whole form, and recommends localized subscription, register over Controller, and virtualization past ~1000 fields.

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/react-hook-form/discussions/11942
sources.claim: Community consensus for RHF async uniqueness checks: keep the remote check out of the Zod resolver; run it via useWatch + debounce + AbortController and surface it with setError/clearErrors.

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/arrays
sources.claim: TanStack Form arrays use <form.Field mode="array">, field.pushValue(...) to append, bracket-indexed subfield names, and the official example keys rows by array index.

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/validation
sources.claim: TanStack Form has built-in async validation with per-field asyncDebounceMs, runs sync validators before async ones unless asyncAlways is set, supports form-level validators that write errors onto specific field paths, and accepts any Standard Schema library.

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/linked-fields
sources.claim: TanStack Form models cross-field dependencies declaratively with onChangeListenTo / onBlurListenTo, and warns that mutual listening creates infinite validation loops.

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/reactivity
sources.claim: TanStack Form's re-render model is selector subscriptions: form.Subscribe isolates the re-render to the subscribing children, useSelector re-renders the whole component, and omitting the selector re-renders on every form state change; useStore is deprecated in favour of useSelector.

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/form-groups
sources.claim: TanStack Form's FormGroup / withFieldGroup gives each wizard step its own validators and an onGroupSubmit handler while the values stay in one parent form store.

sources.title: https://github.com/TanStack/form/issues/2090
sources.claim: form.Subscribe re-renders on every form mutation when the selector returns an object or array, because LocalSubscribe compares with Object.is and the selector allocates a fresh reference each time; open since Mar 2026, fix is to pass shallow equality.

sources.title: https://github.com/TanStack/form/issues/2150
sources.claim: Mounting/unmounting <form.Field> scales worse than linearly: ~1300 fields take 10+ seconds and can crash the tab, versus ~200ms for plain inputs (TanStack Form v1.29.1, May 2026).

sources.title: https://github.com/TanStack/form/issues/957
sources.claim: Removing an item from a TanStack Form array inside a conditionally rendered form duplicates the last element ([1,2,3,4] minus item 2 yields [1,3,4,4]) because rows are reconciled by index.

sources.title: https://github.com/TanStack/form/issues/502
sources.claim: Unmounting a TanStack Form field leaves its value, meta and fieldInfo in the form store; form.deleteField is the manual escape hatch.

sources.title: https://github.com/TanStack/form/issues/1133
sources.claim: A TanStack Form field that unmounts while holding a validation error keeps that error in the store and blocks submission.

sources.title: https://conform.guide/complex-structures
sources.claim: Conform addresses nested data with object.property / array[index] name syntax, getFieldset() for objects and getFieldList() for arrays, with a per-item key from field metadata.

sources.title: https://conform.guide/intent-button
sources.claim: Conform mutates field lists through submit-button intents (insert/remove/reorder/update/validate/reset) serialized into the form submitter, so array editing works without JavaScript.

sources.title: https://conform.guide/api/zod/conformZodMessage
sources.claim: Conform's async-validation pattern builds the Zod schema from the submission intent: the client emits VALIDATION_SKIPPED for untargeted fields and VALIDATION_UNDEFINED when the async check is unavailable, which makes the server re-run it with parseWithZod({ async: true }).

sources.title: https://conform.guide/validation
sources.claim: Conform can run the server schema on every input/blur, not just submit, via shouldValidate / shouldRevalidate, and deliberately has no client-side async validation — it falls back to the server instead of hitting a side endpoint.

sources.title: https://conform.guide/api/react/future/PreserveBoundary
sources.claim: Because Conform reads values from the DOM, unmounted fields lose their values; PreserveBoundary re-injects them and is the sanctioned fix for multi-step wizards, dialogs and virtualized lists.

sources.title: https://github.com/edmundhung/conform/releases
sources.claim: PreserveBoundary shipped in Conform v1.17.0; v1.19.4 (Jun 2026) patched a denial-of-service in the future parseSubmission API triggered by submissions with many repeated fields.

sources.title: https://splitforms.com/blog/best-react-form-library-2026
sources.claim: Bundle sizes measured May 2026 with esbuild: RHF ~9 kB core / ~14 kB with Zod; TanStack Form ~6 kB / ~11 kB; Formik ~13 kB / ~18 kB (min+gzip).

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/comparison
sources.claim: TanStack Form's own comparison table claims ✅ for built-in async debounce and granular per-field subscriptions where React Hook Form is ❓, and flags RHF nested field arrays as ✅*(1) — requiring TypeScript casts.

sources.title: https://zenn.dev/ashunar0/articles/692920ecb633fb?locale=en
sources.claim: RHF v7's mutable-ref + getter-based formState subscription is structurally incompatible with the React Compiler: memoization never invalidates, so watch() goes stale and errors stop updating; 'use no memo' is the v7 workaround.

sources.title: https://conform.guide/api/react/useInputControl
sources.claim: Conform's useInputControl adapts custom/controlled widgets, but resets the value whenever the field key changes — which is exactly what insert/remove/reorder intents do.

sources.title: https://github.com/react-hook-form/react-hook-form
sources.claim: React Hook Form star count and latest v7 release (7.81.0, Jul 5 2026).

sources.title: https://github.com/TanStack/form
sources.claim: TanStack Form star count and active v1.30.x release train (Jul 2026).

sources.title: https://github.com/edmundhung/conform
sources.claim: Conform star count and latest release (1.19.4, Jun 2026).

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/react-hook-form/discussions/9672
sources.claim: Drag-and-drop over nested RHF field arrays breaks when a single ref holds the reorder function: appending a new nested array overwrites it and only the last array reorders; keep a list of reorder callbacks instead.

sources.title: https://claritydev.net/blog/advanced-multistep-forms-with-react
sources.claim: A common RHF wizard pattern gives each step its own useForm with defaultValues seeded from a React context store, and defers cross-step validation to a final confirmation step.

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/react-hook-form/discussions/4028
sources.claim: The community-standard RHF per-step gate is a per-step schema object plus await trigger(fieldNames) before advancing, with shouldUnregister:false keeping values across steps.
